title: API Gateway quota enforcement regression — 429 storm postmortem and remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: On 2026-03-02 a cascade of 429 responses started across multiple customer routes for ~47 minutes due to a regression in the API gateway quota enforcement path that amplified request rejection for both public and internal keys. This ticket records the incident timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and tracked remediation action items.
impact_summary: ~8% of requests to hosted inference API returned 429 over a rolling 10-minute window at peak. Several high-volume customers experienced client-side retries that increased backend load; three paying customers reported degraded service and opened support tickets. Estimated lost traffic: ~62M tokens; estimated revenue impact: medium-term (pending CS follow-up).
timeline: 2026-03-02T10:03Z - Alerts triggered: elevated 429 rate on /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings routes (SLO breach detection)
2026-03-02T10:07Z - Pager duty escalation: platform on-call (Marcus Lee) and API infra (Nora Chen) join incident bridge
2026-03-02T10:12Z - Initial mitigation: applied temporary global rate-limit relax on edge cluster (10% capacity bump). 429s reduced but persisted
2026-03-02T10:25Z - Root cause suspected: recent quota enforcement refactor (gateway-2.4.1) interacting with auth-token caching TTL leading to double-accounting of tokens
2026-03-02T10:38Z - Hotfix deployed: revert commit 4f2b9e (quota-routing change) to gateway-2.3.9 logic; rollback confirmed, 429 rate returned to baseline by 10:50Z
2026-03-03T09:00Z - Postmortem investigation begun; logs, flame graphs, and gateway metrics collected for analysis
2026-03-05T16:00Z - Initial draft of this postmortem completed; action items assigned
root_cause: A regression introduced in gateway-2.4.1 changed the quota routing evaluation order. For authenticated requests the new path attempted to consult both route-specific and service-wide token buckets in quick succession without normalizing a shared counter. Under bursty traffic this produced double-accounting and immediate saturation of token buckets, causing a 429 amplification loop. Additionally, an auth cache TTL misconfiguration made some internal keys repeatedly revalidate, increasing load during the window.
contributing_factors: Deploy merged without full canary in multi-tenant edge: gateway-2.4.1 was rolled to all edge nodes in <10 minutes
Unit tests covered algorithm invariants but not the multi-bucket interaction scenario
Runbook lacked a documented quick rollback path for quota/routing regressions
Auth token cache TTL change was bundled in same release and insufficiently isolated
immediate_mitigation: Temporary global rate-limit relaxation on affected clusters (+10% capacity)
Rollback of gatekeeping commit (reverted quota-routing logic to 2.3.9 behavior)
Communication to affected customers: incident notification and interim RCA note
corrective_actions: A1: Add a deterministic ordering test harness for multi-bucket quota evaluation (owner: Priya Singh; due: 2026-03-14)
A2: Add end-to-end integration test that simulates bursty multi-tenant traffic and validates no double-accounting (owner: Eng QoE team — Nora Chen; due: 2026-03-18)
A3: Update release process: require 15% canary for edge-critical releases and a 30-minute observation gate before full rollout (owner: Platform Releases — Damian Ortiz; due: 2026-03-22)
A4: Separate auth cache TTL change into its own release; add feature-flag gating for cache experiments (owner: Security/Infra — Luis Gomez; due: 2026-03-20)
A5: Runbook updates: add a dedicated section for quota/regression rollback steps and a list of metrics to monitor (owner: SRE — Kelsey Martin; due: 2026-03-12)

A6: Dashboard and alert tuning: add synthetic checks that validate correct token-bucket invariants and an automated alert when double-accounting ratio > 0.01 (owner: Observability — Chen Wu; due: 2026-03-16)
A7: Customer remediation: CS to reach out to top 5 impacted accounts with usage-impact report and credit proposal (owner: Customer Success — Maya Kapoor; due: 2026-03-11)
A8: Security review of quota codepath changes to ensure no auth bypass/chaining edge cases (owner: Security — Elena Ferris; due: 2026-03-14)
A9: Post-release retrospective and blameless review session to capture learnings and process changes (owner: Incident Lead — Marcus Lee; due: 2026-03-15)
A10: Implement feature-flagged rollout for quota algorithm changes with automatic rollback on metric regression (owner: Platform — Damian Ortiz; due: 2026-04-01)

acceptance_criteria: All corrective actions A1-A6 implemented and merged to main
New integration test prevents regressions (CI green on 3 consecutive runs)
Canary gating added to release pipeline and demonstrated in one non-critical release
Security review completed and signed off
Customer communications sent and CS tickets closed or acknowledged
follow_up_notes: We observed that retries from client SDKs amplified the 429 storm; as part of A2 we will include a client-retry-aware simulation. Consider advisory to SDK teams to implement exponential backoff with jitter if not already present. Ticket will be revisited after A10 rollout for long-term validation.
